PENNSYLVANIA GRADUATION RATES REPORTING REGULATION

Pursuant to the Pennsylvania Graduation Rates Reporting Act, 24 P.S. Section 2502.5, this regulation establishes comprehensive requirements for the collection, calculation, and reporting of graduation rate data by all public educational institutions in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.

SECTION 1: DEFINITIONS

For purposes of this regulation:

(a) "Cohort" means a group of first-time, full-time degree-seeking undergraduate students who enter an institution during the same academic year.

(b) "Graduation rate" means the percentage of students in a cohort who complete their program of study within 150% of the normal time for program completion.

(c) "Institution" means any public secondary school, community college, state-related university, or state-owned university in Pennsylvania.

(d) "Normal time" means four years for a bachelor's degree, two years for an associate degree, and the published length of the program for other degrees and certificates.

(e) "Retention rate" means the percentage of first-time undergraduate students who return to the same institution for their second year of study.

SECTION 2: REPORTING REQUIREMENTS

All covered institutions shall submit annual graduation rate reports to the Pennsylvania Department of Education containing the following elements:

(a) Overall institutional graduation rates calculated using the cohort method, disaggregated by:
- Full-time and part-time enrollment status
- Gender
- Race and ethnicity categories as defined by federal reporting standards
- First-generation college student status
- Pell Grant recipient status
- In-state versus out-of-state residency

(b) Program-specific graduation rates for each degree program offered, including:
- Certificate programs
- Associate degree programs
- Bachelor's degree programs
- Graduate and professional programs

(c) Retention rates using the same demographic disaggregation as graduation rates.

(d) Transfer-out rates for students who did not graduate but subsequently enrolled at another institution.

(e) Employment outcomes data for graduates, including:
- Employment rates within six months and one year of graduation
- Average starting salaries by program
- Employment in field of study rates

SECTION 3: DATA COLLECTION AND METHODOLOGY

Institutions shall:

(a) Maintain comprehensive student records tracking academic progress from enrollment through completion or departure.

(b) Use the cohort methodology consistent with federal IPEDS reporting standards, tracking students who begin as first-time, full-time degree-seeking undergraduates.

(c) Exclude from cohort calculations students who die, become permanently disabled, leave to serve in the armed forces, leave to serve on official church missions, or leave to serve with a foreign aid service of the federal government.

(d) Include transfer students in calculations only for retention rate purposes, not graduation rate calculations.

(e) Verify data accuracy through internal auditing processes and maintain supporting documentation for all reported figures.

SECTION 4: REPORTING TIMELINE AND SUBMISSION

Institutions shall submit graduation rate reports according to the following schedule:

(a) Annual reports are due to the Department of Education no later than March 15 of each year, covering data from the previous academic year ending June 30.

(b) Preliminary data may be submitted by February 1 for review and feedback from the Department.

(c) Corrections or revisions to previously submitted data must be submitted within 30 days of discovery of errors.

(d) Supplementary employment outcomes data shall be submitted by September 15, allowing additional time for graduate follow-up surveys.

SECTION 5: PUBLIC DISCLOSURE

The Department of Education shall:

(a) Compile and publish an annual statewide report summarizing graduation rates across all institutions by December 1 of each year.

(b) Make individual institutional reports available to the public through the Department's website within 45 days of receipt.

(c) Provide comparative analyses showing trends over time and benchmarking against national averages where available.

(d) Protect individual student privacy in accordance with FERPA requirements while maximizing transparency of institutional performance.

SECTION 6: ACCOUNTABILITY AND COMPLIANCE

Institutions failing to submit complete and accurate reports by required deadlines may face:

(a) Formal notification of non-compliance with requirement to cure deficiencies within 30 days.

(b) Withholding of state appropriations until compliance is achieved.

(c) Public designation as non-compliant with state reporting requirements.

(d) Required development of institutional improvement plans addressing factors contributing to low graduation rates.

SECTION 7: TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE

The Department shall provide ongoing technical assistance to institutions including standardized reporting templates, training workshops, and consultation on data collection methodologies to ensure consistent and accurate reporting across all institutions.

This regulation shall take effect 60 days after publication and apply to all graduation rate reports submitted thereafter.
enhanced.summary: This regulation implements Pennsylvania's Graduation Rates Reporting Act, requiring all public educational institutions to submit comprehensive annual reports on graduation and retention rates. Reports must include demographic breakdowns, program-specific data, and employment outcomes. Institutions must use standardized cohort methodology and submit reports by March 15 annually. The Department of Education will compile statewide summaries and make data publicly available. Non-compliance may result in withheld state funding and required improvement plans.
requirements: Submit annual graduation rate reports with demographic disaggregation by gender, race, ethnicity, first-generation status, and financial aid status
Provide program-specific graduation rates for all degree and certificate programs offered by the institution
Report retention rates, transfer-out rates, and employment outcomes data for graduates within specified timeframes
Use standardized cohort methodology consistent with federal IPEDS reporting standards for data calculation
Maintain comprehensive student tracking systems and supporting documentation for all reported graduation rate data
